title: Granny Cake (Appalachian Pineapple Cake)
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Grease a 13x9-inch baking dish.
Whisk together granulated sugar, flour, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
Add eggs and the undrained crushed pineapple; mix until smooth.
Pour batter into the prepared baking dish and spread evenly. Sprinkle walnuts and brown sugar evenly over the top.
Bake 45-50 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out with a few moist crumbs.

With about 10 minutes left on the bake time, make the glaze: combine evaporated milk, granulated sugar, and butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a gentle boil, boil 1 minute, remove from heat, and stir in vanilla extract.
Pour the warm glaze over the cake while it is still warm. Cool slightly or completely before serving.
notes: Sent as a Facebook reel by Josh Addair, captioned as a recipe recommended by 'The Twang Sistas' — a classic Appalachian dessert with flour, sugar, crushed pineapple, eggs, brown sugar, walnuts, and an evaporated milk glaze. The exact Twang Sistas recipe text wasn't retrievable from the reel or its top comments (1,500+ comments, mostly reactions/anecdotes, no posted recipe found), so ingredient amounts and steps are filled in from a closely matching standard Granny Cake recipe with the same ingredient profile. Swap walnuts for pecans or almonds if preferred. Don't drain the pineapple — the juice keeps the cake moist. Pour the glaze on while the cake is still warm so it soaks in.
